title.narrative: NESA Center Security Opportunities in the MENA Region Forum 01-23

description.narrative: From 1618 August, a collection of partnered institutions from the Quad member states conducted the first Quad Critical and Emerging Technology Forum in San Diego, California. The forum had thirty-one participants representing industry, research laboratories, academic institutions, and government departments/ministries from each of the Quad member states. The forum was organized around three pillars: intra-Quad cooperation in critical and emerging technologies, Quad technological support for the Indo-Pacific, and Quad efforts in domain awareness and information sharing. Conversations amongst the participants covered artificial intelligence, quantum computing, STEM workforce development, public-private partnerships, information sharing, cybersecurity, and countering disinformation in detail. A second iteration of the forum will occur in 2024 to continue refining ideas, proposals, and recommendations. The report that follows provides notable data points from conversations, along with a set of recommendations for Quad member states, specific industries, and research institutions.

description.narrative: The United States welcomes the opportunity to host Negev Forum members in Washington, DC for a series of discussions on regional security, cooperation opportunities, and information sharing. This seminar will provide a venue for participants to explore and identify areas of cooperation and disagreement, and develop proposals to promote progress. The seminar will allow the participants to hear different viewpoints and establish personal relationships. Participants will also constructively explore ways to enhance cooperation among their countries and build trust to advance strategic national interests. The program will include participants from Negev partner countries from the defense, security and diplomatic establishment.

title.narrative: NESA Center Arab-Israeli Conflict: Israel/Jordan Trust to Enhance Defense & Security Cooperation Seminar 01-21

description.narrative: The objective of this series seeks to build trust and strengthen cooperation between Israel and its Arab neighbors. The series will begin with a seminar on Israel and Jordan. Both have a stake in solving the Palestinian issue, curbing Iranian influence, countering extremist and radical forces, and achieving regional stability. Both are major non-NATO allies of the United States and cooperate with Washington on critical defense and intelligence issues. Jordan is the second Arab country after Egypt to sign a peace treaty with Israel, yet faces growing domestic pressure to terminate the treaty in the absence of a settlement with the Palestinian issue. This seminar seeks to explain and analyze these issues. By hearing different viewpoints, participants will have a firm basis to explore ways to advance cooperation and strengthen trust as a strategic national interest for all parties.

title.narrative: Near East South Asia Center / Africa Command Workshop 01-23: "Changing Nature of Security, Warfare, Institutions and Players"

description.narrative: The group will examine theoretical threats and how best to develop capabilities and strategies to address new technologies, insurgency and hybrid conflicts, and non-traditional security demands. Discussions will include challenges that range from cyber, anti-access, criminal elements to transnational, malign players, and the super-empowered non-state actors. Lastly, the group will look at the impact of grey/hybrid warfare and the convergence of technologies that directly impact how we organize, how we fight and more importantly what we can expect from enemy states, as well as non-state actors. The objective is to lay out the extent of the problem, but more importantly address existing initiatives taken nationally and regionally and propose new regional initiatives with inputs/insights from "whole of government" and "whole of society" in a venue for USAFRICOM, senior security professionals, and young security experts to discuss security requirements, protocols, processes and policies to address/brainstorm required institutional, organizational, and cultural changes under Chatham House rule of non-attribution.
